{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Dov I. Levine''' ({{Langx|he|דב לוין}}; born July 19, 1958) is an American-Israeli physicist, known for his research on [[quasicrystal]]s,<ref name=BuckleyPrize>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Levine&first_nm=Dov&year=2010|title=2010 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize Recipient, Dov Levine|website=American Physical Society}}</ref> soft condensed matter physics (including granular materials, emulsions, and foams), and statistical mechanics out of equilibrium.<ref name=aip>{{cite web|title=D. Levine, Biography|website=American Institute of Physics|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11605011.html}}</ref>

==Education and career==
The son of a professor of physical chemistry, Dov Levine grew up in New York.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KPqac4Y551AC&pg=PA169| page=169 |title=In Our Own Image: Personal Symmetry in Discovery | isbn=978-0-306-46091-3 | last1=Hargittai | first1=Istvan | last2=Hargittai | first2=Magdolna | date=29 February 2000 | publisher=Springer }}</ref> He graduated in 1979 with a B.S. from [[Stony Brook University]] and in 1986 with a Ph.D. in physics from the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. His Ph.D. thesis ''Quasicrystals: A New Class of Ordered Structure'' was supervised by [[Paul Steinhardt]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dov Levine|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=776783}}</ref>

In 1981, Levine and Steinhardt began developing their theory of a hypothetical new form of matter with icosahedral symmetry (or other forbidden symmetries) that violated the century-old laws of crystallography.  The idea, motivated by their study of Penrose tilings,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Penrose | first1 = R. | year = 1974 | title = The role of aesthetics in pure and applied mathematical research| url = https://docplayer.net/6619518-1-r-penrose-the-role-of-aesthetics-in-pure-and-applied-mathematical-research-bull-inst-math-appl-10-1974-266-271.html | journal = Bulletin of the Institute of Mathematics and Its Applications | volume = 10 | issue = | pages = 266–271  | doi =  | bibcode= | doi-access =  }}</ref> was to consider atomic arrangements that are quasiperiodic rather than periodic.  They introduced the term quasicrystals, short for quasiperiodic crystal, to describe the idea.  Independently, in April 1982,  while studying an aluminum-manganese alloy, A6Mn, [[Dan Shechtman]] made a scientific observation, published in 1984, of "a metallic solid which diffracts electrons like a single crystal but has a point group symmetry (icosahedral) that is inconsistent with lattice translations."<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Shechtman | first1 = D. | last2 = Blech | first2 = I.| last3 = Gratias | first3 = D. | last4 = Cahn | first4 = J.W. | year = 1984 | title = Metallic Phase with Long-Range Orientational Order and No Translational Symmetry | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett. | volume = 53 | issue = 20 | pages = 1951–1953 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1951 | bibcode=1984PhRvL..53.1951S| doi-access = free }}</ref> When Levine and Steinhardt were shown a preprint, they recognized the diffraction pattern as matching their prediction for an icosahedral quasicrystal and, hence, published their theory and proposed that explanation.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Levine | first1 = D. | last2 = Steinhardt | first2 = P.J. | year = 1984 | title = Quasicrystals: A New Class of Ordered Structures | url = http://physics.princeton.edu/~steinh/LevineSteinhardt1.pdf | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett. | volume = 53 | issue = 26 | pages = 2477–2480  | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.2477 | bibcode=1984PhRvL..53.2477L| doi-access = free }}</ref>

According to Steinhardt:
{{blockquote|Quasicrystals are quasiperiodic structures with an arrangement described by a sum of two or more [[periodic function]]s whose periods have a ratio equal to an [[irrational number]]; so, they are precisely described like a crystal but in a non-repeating pattern, like a [[glass]].<ref>{{cite book|title=In Our Own Image: Personal Symmetry in Discovery|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KPqac4Y551AC&pg=PA173|page=173| isbn=978-0-306-46091-3 | last1=Hargittai | first1=Istvan | last2=Hargittai | first2=Magdolna | date=29 February 2000 | publisher=Springer }}</ref>}}

Levine was from 1986 to 1988 a postdoctoral member of [[UCSB]]'s [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics|ITP (now known as KIPT)]] and from 1988 to 1989 a visiting scientist at the Weizmann Institute. He was from 1988 to 1991 an assistant professor at the [[University of Florida]]. In 1990 he joined the physics department of the [[Technion]],<ref name=aip/> where he is now a professor of physics.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dov Levine|website=Department of Physics, the Technion|url=https://phys.technion.ac.il/en/people/faculty/person/47}}</ref> For the academic year 1997–1998 he was a visiting member of UCSB's ITP.<ref name=aip/>

In 2020 he published, with [[Shankar Ghosh (physicist)|Shankar Ghosh]] and five other colleagues, research on the development of rechargeable [[N95 mask]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1063/5.0023940|title=Recharging and rejuvenation of decontaminated N95 masks |year=2020 |last1=Hossain |first1=Emroj |last2=Bhadra |first2=Satyanu |last3=Jain |first3=Harsh |last4=Das |first4=Soumen |last5=Bhattacharya |first5=Arnab |last6=Ghosh |first6=Shankar |last7=Levine |first7=Dov |journal=Physics of Fluids |volume=32 |issue=9 |page=093304 |pmid=32982134 |pmc=7513826 |arxiv=2004.13641 |bibcode=2020PhFl...32i3304H }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Coldewey, Devin|date=14 September 2020|title=N95 masks could soon be rechargeable instead of disposable|website=yahoo! news|url=https://ph.news.yahoo.com/n95-masks-could-soon-rechargeable-225632070.html}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* [[National Science Foundation]] [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]]<ref name=BuckleyPrize/>
* Alon Fellowship at [[Tel Aviv University]]<ref name=BuckleyPrize/>
* Minoru and Ethel Tsutsui Distinguished Graduate Research Award from the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=BuckleyPrize/>
* With [[Paul Steinhardt]] and [[Alan Mackay (physicist)|Alan Mackay]], the [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]]<ref name=BuckleyPrize/>
* 2021 Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2021&unit_id=&institution=Technion}} (search on year=2021 and institution=Technion)</ref>
